stories.summary: Mumbai: Six in 10 Indian consumers trust artificial intelligence (AI) and online health information as much as advice from health care professionals, according to a new study by Boston Consulting Group (BCG). The findings point to changing expectations among Indian consumers, who are seeking greater

stories.title: BCG report finds healthcare is becoming a commodity
stories.summary: Nearly half of global consumers view healthcare products as standard consumer goods, according to a Boston Consulting Group report. Roughly two-thirds of surveyed patients now demand greater control over costs and treatment choices, expecting the same convenience from medical providers that they currently receive from retail businesses.

stories.title: PLI schemes miss employment targets
stories.summary: India’s production-linked incentive schemes have generated 849,069 jobs, reaching 28 percent of the three million target by FY26. While investments reached 76 percent of the goal and production hit 64 percent, the schemes have struggled to convert manufacturing expansion into large-scale hiring. The jobs are still pending.

stories.title: KPMG outlines food system transformation priorities
stories.summary: KPMG India has identified six levers for food system transformation, including supply chain excellence, technology enablement and sustainability-led growth. The report, Future of Food Systems, notes that changing consumption patterns and climate pressures are reshaping the ecosystem, while highlighting an ongoing gap in affordability and nutrition for many.

stories.title: Telecom sector faces complex regulatory shift
stories.summary: The telecommunications industry is entering a transformation phase driven by AI, 5G and satellite connectivity. A new white paper notes that regulators and service providers must adapt to support investment and competition, as digital operating models continue to reshape how services are built, delivered and governed globally.

stories.title: India ranked as AI rising contender
stories.summary: Boston Consulting Group has named India an AI Rising Contender in its 2026 maturity matrix. The report identifies India’s growing pool of skilled talent as its primary advantage over computing infrastructure, placing the nation among economies with high readiness to adopt AI but lower exposure to immediate disruption.

stories.title: Banks move to control AI agent costs
stories.summary: Global banks are forming AI FinOps teams to manage costs associated with AI agents, which could reach 20 percent of total labor expenses. McKinsey’s annual review notes that initial efforts to route queries to different models based on complexity have proven less effective than anticipated at curbing spending.

stories.title: BRG adds senior advisor and directors
stories.summary: Management consulting firm BRG has hired Punam Anand Keller as a senior advisor alongside new managing directors Marcus Leach and Josh Hesterman. Keller, a faculty member at the Tuck School of Business, specializes in consumer decision-making and will join the firm's consumer protection and product liability practice.

stories.title: EY Australia establishes independent oversight
stories.summary: EY Australia has launched an independent Oceania Public Interest Council to strengthen governance. The move follows regulatory pressure and warnings from KPMG regarding the failure of previous external inquiries to uncover evidence. The council will feature a majority of independent members to challenge firm management.

stories.title: Haldiram Snacks appoints EY for IPO
stories.summary: Haldiram Snacks Food has appointed EY to manage its 10,000 crore rupee initial public offering. The company is reportedly targeting a valuation of 1 lakh crore rupees by 2027. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Mother-son duo builds millet business
stories.summary: A mother-son duo has launched Mighty Millets, a venture supplying luxury hotels. The business follows the founders' previous experience at KPMG and their move into kitchen labs. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Deloitte recruits KPMG restructuring team
stories.summary: Deloitte has hired KPMG Australia’s national turnaround and restructuring leader Tim Mableson, along with partners James Dampney and Peter Gothard. The group, which previously worked at Ferrier Hodgson, joins Deloitte as the accounting firm continues to lose senior personnel to its competitors.

stories.title: Marsh to acquire investment consultancy Wilshire
stories.summary: Marsh has agreed to buy Wilshire, an investment consulting and analytics firm, from Motive Partners and CC Capital. Wilshire manages 221 billion dollars in assets and advises on 1.6 trillion dollars more. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

stories.title: KPMG Pakistan leaves global network
stories.summary: KPMG’s Pakistani member firm has left the global network to operate as Taseer Hadi Khalid and Co. The separation followed disagreements over plans to centralize regional management. The firm, which joined the network in 1987, confirmed that its clients and ongoing engagements will remain in place.

stories.title: Marsh expands investment business with Wilshire deal
stories.summary: Marsh will acquire Wilshire to expand its reach into the financial adviser-led wealth market. The deal adds 221 billion dollars in assets under management and 1.6 trillion dollars under advisement to Marsh's portfolio, providing clients with new access to model portfolios, indexes and data analytics.

stories.title: Ex-PwC partners report rapid revenue growth
stories.summary: Horizon Nexus Partners, launched by former PwC partners Rob Silverwood and Sanjiv Jeraj, reports 100 million Australian dollars in revenue after 12 months. Backed by BGH Capital, the firm aims to build an accounting business worth up to 500 million Australian dollars within five years.

stories.title: Harbor acquires AAC Consulting
stories.summary: Managed legal services provider Harbor has acquired AAC Consulting, a firm specializing in Aderant financial management software. The deal aims to enhance Harbor's ability to assist law firms with revenue cycle management, including billing, systems assessments and data conversion projects.

stories.title: eClerx acquires RegEdge
stories.summary: eClerx Services has acquired RegEdge, a boutique firm focused on risk and regulatory services for financial institutions. The acquisition is intended to deepen eClerx’s expertise in AI-powered analytics and automation, helping clients navigate complex regulatory requirements within the financial sector.

stories.title: AM Consulting Engineers completes second acquisition
stories.summary: Belfast-based AM Consulting Engineers has acquired Haworth McCall, a structural and civil engineering firm with teams in Brighton and Belfast. This is the consultancy's second acquisition in less than a year, following its purchase of Bridges Pound, as it continues to expand its UK operations.

stories.title: Indian mutual funds increase Nvidia exposure
stories.summary: Thirteen Indian mutual fund schemes and ETFs held direct exposure to Nvidia in their October portfolios, with allocations reaching up to 12.12 percent of assets. A senior government official suggested that the recent 30 percent share-price plunge could benefit Indian IT services firms. Markets remain optimistic about volatility.

stories.title: India remains world's largest edible oil importer
stories.summary: NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri stated that India meets over half of its edible oil needs through imports. These imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at approximately $20 billion. The country is still not secure regarding its food supply across various products.

stories.title: Accenture rolls out bonuses while holding promotions
stories.summary: Accenture has begun issuing performance bonuses in India, with top performers receiving up to 26 percent of fixed pay. The company has kept broad-based promotions on hold, shifting toward a centralized compensation structure that limits permanent salary increases. The bonus cycle is now the primary path for compensation.

stories.title: TVS Supply Chain Results Approved
stories.summary: TVS Supply Chain Solutions Limited announced the approval of its unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. The board also appointed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP as the company’s internal auditor for the financial year 2026-27.

stories.title: MECON and Ernst and Young sign investment MoU
stories.summary: MECON Limited has signed a memorandum of understanding with Ernst and Young LLP to collaborate on investment attraction and economic development services. The partnership focuses on supporting industrial and infrastructure growth. Both organizations aim to facilitate investment processes through this strategic cooperation.

stories.summary: Students pursuing careers in investment banking and consulting now face an accelerated recruitment process. Applications that once opened during junior year now begin as early as sophomore year. Yale University predicts that bulge bracket firms will continue to pull recruitment timelines forward for those seeking future roles.

stories.title: Booth student shares consulting recruitment experience
stories.summary: Elliott T. Raia, co-chair of the Management Consulting Group at Chicago Booth, says there is a high probability that someone in the group shares your background and will help you recruit. He notes that Financial Statement Analysis and Consumer Behavior provided him with tangible skills. Recruitment is collaborative.

stories.title: Report lists top 10 chartered accountancy firms in India
stories.summary: Chartered accountancy firms in India provide services ranging from statutory audits and taxation to forensic accounting and business restructuring. These firms serve a client base including startups, multinational corporations, and government agencies. The industry remains a diverse mix of international networks and large Indian firms.

stories.title: Consulting firms in India focus on digital transformation
stories.summary: The business consulting sector in India is expanding as organizations seek guidance on strategy, sustainability, and operational excellence. Firms operating in the country claim to combine global methodologies with deep local market understanding to support large enterprises and emerging businesses. Growth is the stated goal.

stories.title: PwC promotes Soumya Roy Choudhury to director
stories.summary: PwC Acceleration Center India has promoted Soumya Roy Choudhury to director of talent acquisition. In his new role, he will focus on strengthening recruitment as a strategic business advisory function and developing technology-enabled solutions. He has spent the last decade with the firm.

stories.title: Marine Corps veteran discusses consulting path at Booth
stories.summary: Kolby Haas, a second-year MBA student at Chicago Booth and co-chair of the Armed Forces Group, is transitioning from the US Marine Corps into management consulting. He says the school stands out as a top pick for veterans. The military experience is now being applied to strategy.

stories.title: Qantas to outsource 850 corporate roles to Accenture
stories.summary: Qantas will outsource 850 corporate positions to Accenture as part of a restructuring plan, with most services delivered from India. The airline also confirmed nearly 1,000 job cuts, including mass redundancies. The arrangement is intended to redesign the airline's corporate operations and workforce structure.

research.title: Huge If True: Learning from the Size of the Surprise
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Responses to earnings surprises depend on an unknown multiplier mapping earnings to value. Investors, however, learn about the news and the multiplier from the same number. Large surprises may indicate small multipliers and tiny surprises large. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is no best worker in general, only a best worker for a particular firm. We develop a measure of worker-firm match quality that treats fit as a property of the pair, learned from the survival. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Incomplete-market CAPM equilibria in continuous time
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study continuous-time CAPM equilibria with general mean-variance preferences of the form $U(\mu,\sigma)$, where $U$ is strictly quasiconcave, increasing in the mean $\mu$ and decreasing in the volatility $\sigma$ of terminal wealth. Our framework accommodates both. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Individualized Algorithmic Advice as a Strategic Signal on Competitive Markets
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As algorithms increasingly mediate competitive decision-making, their influence extends beyond individual outcomes to shaping strategic market dynamics. In our experiment, we examined how algorithmic advice affects human behavior in a classic economic game with a unique. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Optimizing Bidding Curves for Renewable Energy in Two-Settlement Electricity Markets
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coordination of day-ahead and real-time electricity markets is imperative for cost-effective electricity supply and also to provide efficient incentives for the energy transition. Although stochastic market designs feature the least-cost coordination, they are incompatible with current. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: People escalate against a competitor labelled human and hold back against one labelled an optimising machine
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: People increasingly compete against AI agents, and organisations decide what to tell them about these opponents. We distinguish an opponent effect, specific to the system faced, from an information effect, a property of the disclosure. In. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Perceived Social Norms and Information Disclosure
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Social-information messages are widely used to influence norm perceptions and norm-relevant behavior, but their effects may depend on what they report and how they are disclosed. This paper develops a belief-based framework connecting personal values and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Price co-movement and price information diverge across Nordic electricity zones after the energy crisis
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: After the 2021-2022 energy crisis, day-ahead prices in Nordic bidding zones no longer move together. We ask whether this divergence also changes the information carried by prices. The answer matters for integrating variable renewable energy (VRE). Preprint, not peer reviewed.
